_help: Moderation for the public issue tracker, applied on every deploy. Each action runs once (tracked by its unique id; never reuse one). op: close | reopen | delete. Example: { "id": "2026-11-05-close-12", "op": "close", "issue": 12, "resolution": "Fixed in v0.7.9" }

actions.resolution: Fixed in v0.8.3: agent commands on macOS/Linux now run as one unit between output markers, so output is no longer dropped, garbled or mixed with shell prompts.
Fixed in v0.8.3: a task paused on a long-running tool is no longer evicted from the chat view, so its history stays visible.
Fixed in v0.8.3: ask_user questions render markdown, and replies split into several text blocks keep their formatting.
Fixed in v0.8.3: stale thinking blocks are dropped by the API after a model or effort switch instead of failing the request.
Fixed in source, ships in the next release: {a,b} alternatives now work in grep_search include/exclude and in glob patterns, and an invalid pattern returns an error instead of matching nothing.
Duplicate of #9. Inline strings were not the cause; the workbook's table relationship was.
Fixed in source, ships in the next release: absolute worksheet relationship targets (as openpyxl writes them) are rewritten to the relative form before the workbook is parsed.

Fixed in source, ships in the next release: the end marker is stripped even when long output pushed the begin marker out of the captured tail, and a shell-exit notice no longer repeats output that was already returned.
Fixed in source, ships in the next release: string arguments are converted to the number, boolean, array or object type the tool's schema declares before the MCP call.
Fixed in source, ships in the next release: workbooks with openpyxl-style comment parts now open. The comments themselves are not displayed.

Fixed in source, ships in the next release: file changes are now recorded for every running task instead of only the one that started last, and a file another task wrote with an edit tool is no longer credited to a task whose command was running at the time. Wrong entries recorded before the fix are not cleaned up.

Fixed in source, ships in the next release: agent terminals are closed about 30 seconds after their command finishes, and a read after that failed. A closed terminal's last output now stays readable, and the finish notice no longer says a closed terminal is still open.

Fixed in source, ships in v0.8.6: include and exclude were matched against the file's absolute path, so only patterns starting with a wildcard could match. They now match the project-relative path, the path relative to the search directory, or the bare file name. Directories above the project no longer take part in matching.

Fixed in source, ships in v0.8.6: the four theme tools were defined but missing from the built-in tool list, so calls were sent to MCP. They are now routed to their handler, and a test fails for any future tool that is defined but not routed.

Fixed in source, ships in v0.8.6: the echo of Rustic's command wrapper is now cut out of the raw output before it is cleaned up, wherever the line wraps, and is hidden in the rendered screen view too. Not covered: a wrapper echo longer than 64 KB.

Fixed in source, ships in v0.8.6: the 256 KB limit on ranged reads is gone. A range is streamed from the file, so the cost is the window and not the file size. The cap on how much text one read returns is unchanged.

Fixed in source, ships in v0.8.6: closed agent terminals now have their shell terminated and collected instead of being left behind, a deleted chat closes its agent terminals, and the app raises its open-file limit at startup (macOS starts apps at 256).
Fixed in source, ships in v0.8.6: files that cannot be opened are reported. If nothing could be read the search returns an error, otherwise the result says it is incomplete and lists up to ten paths.

Fixed in source, ships in v0.8.6: an agent that cannot finish a goal can end its turn with a blocked marker and a reason. The loop then stops without an evaluator pass and the goal shows as blocked with that reason. Sending a message clears the goal; a new /goal starts the loop again. A turn cap and repetition detection were not added.

Fixed in source, ships in v0.8.6. The cause was not image caching: when one response held a command followed by a file read, every read ran before the command, so the read saw the file from before it was rewritten (or not yet created). Reads sent after a write or command now run after it, in the order sent.
